spec.description: Download counts for your Docker Hub and GHCR images over the dashboard time range, grouped per package, with package and collector views. The counts are requests, not people or finished downloads, and on GHCR an automated manifest read counts too.

spec.title: Package downloads in ${span} ${spanunit}
spec.description: Every tracked package ranked by downloads in the dashboard time range, with a bar that compares them, in a list that scrolls. Docker Hub and GHCR are added together unless Split by registry is on, which gives each registry its own row. A package tracked for only part of the range counts from its first read.

spec.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_replace(label_replace(round(sum by (owner, repo${split}) (delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m]))), "registry_name", "Docker Hub", "registry", "dockerhub"), "registry_name", "GHCR", "registry", "ghcr"), "package", " · ", "repo", "registry_name"), "package", "$1", "package", "(.*) · ")

spec.title: Downloads per package
spec.description: New downloads of the five most downloaded packages in the dashboard time range, as bars in their own colours, and of every other package together, as a grey line on the right-hand axis. A bar spans an hour on a day or less, a day on 30 days and a week on 6 months, and one below zero means a registry restated its total lower. With Split by registry on, each registry gets its own bars and grey line, the GHCR line dashed. Tall bars after a release are normal, and automated reads move these counts too, because a GHCR manifest read counts as a download.

spec.expr: label_replace(label_join(label_replace(label_replace(((sum by (owner, repo${split}) (delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__interval:1m]))) and on (owner, repo${split}) topk(5, sum by (owner, repo${split}) (delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m] @ end())))), "registry_name", "Docker Hub", "registry", "dockerhub"), "registry_name", "GHCR", "registry", "ghcr"), "package", " · ", "repo", "registry_name"), "package", "$1", "package", "(.*) · ") and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)

spec.title: Downloads in ${span} ${spanunit}
spec.description: Downloads across the selected packages and registries in the dashboard time range, whose length the title names. These are request counts as each registry reports them, so automated reads count too, and a registry that restates its total lower reduces the number. No downloads yet means no package has two reads in the range.

spec.expr: round(sum(delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m])))

spec.title: Change from ${spanthe} ${span} ${spanunit} before
spec.description: Downloads in the dashboard time range against the span of the same length that ends where the range starts, in percent and as the difference in downloads. The percent is green from 0 up, yellow from -20 to 0 and red below -20, and the difference keeps the text colour. A rise with no release behind it usually means an automated reader started polling, and No earlier range yet means the counts do not reach back that far. The percent is left out when the earlier span counted no downloads, common on ranges of a few hours, where each span holds one check or none at the default hourly interval.

spec.expr: round(sum(delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m])))

round(sum(delta((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"}))[$__range:1m] offset $__range))) and (count(last_over_time((max by (owner, repo, registry) (registrystats_image_pulls_total{repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner",registry=~"$registry"} offset $__range))[1d:1h] offset $__range)) > 0)

spec.title: Recent pushes
spec.description: The 3 GHCR packages pushed most recently, newest first, from the "Last published" time each package page shows. Every push moves it, signatures, attestations and branch tags included, so a push is not always a release. Docker Hub publishes no push time, so only GHCR packages are listed. No pushes yet means no package page stated a time.

spec.expr: topk(3, max by (owner, repo) (registrystats_image_last_pushed_timestamp_seconds{registry="ghcr",repo=~"$repo",owner=~"$owner"})) * 1000

spec.title: Registries out of step
spec.description: Packages one registry has and the other definitively lacks at the last complete read, each status naming its collector, and a GHCR name with a slash, which Docker Hub cannot hold, is never compared. An Unknown row shows a stale or incomplete read, or for 7 days a collector that stopped reporting, whatever the time range, because the table shows the state now. With owner/* on both registries, a package you publish to one on purpose stays listed while your configuration covers it. A read counts as stale after 2 hours, which assumes the default hourly check, and No package missing means every read was fresh and complete, which a collector that reads one registry also shows.

spec.title: Checks passed and failed
spec.description: Checks per registry across the selected collectors: passed in blue for Docker Hub and purple for GHCR, failed stacked on top in red and orange. A bar spans an hour on a day or less, 6 hours on a week, a day on 30 days and a week on 6 months, and the legend total adds up the bars. Each collector checks once an hour at the default interval, so no bar means no check finished, and a check at either edge of the range can fall outside the bars. A failed check lost a whole listing or most of its package reads, so any red or orange bar is worth a look at the container log.

(label_replace(label_replace(round(sum by (source) (max by (job, instance, source) (increase(registrystats_collect_errors_total{job=~"$job"}[$__interval])))) > 0, "name", "Docker Hub", "source", "dockerhub"), "name", "GHCR", "source", "ghcr")) and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)

spec.title: Check duration
spec.description: How long a full check of both registries takes, in minutes, as the median and the 95th percentile of the checks in each point's span. A span is an hour on a day or less, 6 hours on a week, a day on 30 days and a week on 6 months. GHCR pages are spaced 2 to 5 seconds apart and Docker Hub requests half a second apart, so the time grows with the number of images. A climb with no new images means slower or retried requests.

spec.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (increase(registrystats_collect_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job"}[$__interval]))) / 60 and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (increase(registrystats_collect_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job"}[$__interval]))) / 60 and on () (vector(time()) > $__from / 1000)

spec.title: Collector not reporting
spec.description: A registry-stats scrape target your Prometheus server cannot scrape now, by its instance, or No collector when no target of the scrape job registry-stats exists. It reads the same two signals as the shipped alerts RegistryStatsTargetDown and RegistryStatsTargetAbsent, which fire once the condition lasts 15 minutes, and like them it needs the scrape job to be called registry-stats. Every other figure is stale until a collector reports again, so check the container and your scrape target.

spec.expr: up{job="registry-stats"} == 0 or label_replace(absent(up{job="registry-stats"}), "instance", "No collector", "", "")

spec.title: Checks stalled
spec.description: A collector that has finished no check for 6 hours while it is still scraped, by its instance. It reads the same signal as the shipped alert RegistryStatsCollectStalled, which fires after the same 6 hours. The collector keeps serving its last counts, so read its container log. In one-shot mode, with POLL_INTERVAL_HOURS at 0, this tile always shows.

spec.expr: (min_over_time((sum by (job, instance) (increase(registrystats_collects_total[15m])) == bool 0)[6h:1m]) == 1) and on (job, instance) (count_over_time((sum by (job, instance) (increase(registrystats_collects_total[15m])) == bool 0)[6h:1m]) > 359)

spec.title: Failed checks in ${span} ${spanunit}
spec.description: Checks that lost a whole listing or most of their package reads in the dashboard time range, per registry, counting every failure of a process that started inside the range. The shipped alert RegistryStatsSourceDegraded reads the same counter, a failure within 3 hours or since a start under 3 hours ago. Checks passed and failed on the Collector health tab shows when, though its bars leave out the newest part of the range, and the container log names the cause.

spec.expr: label_replace(label_replace(round(sum by (source) (max by (job, instance, source) (increase(registrystats_collect_errors_total{source=~"$registry"}[$__range]) or label_replace(registrystats_collect_errors_total{source=~"$registry"} > 0 and on (job, instance) (time() - max by (job, instance) (process_start_time_seconds) < $__range_s), "arm", "start", "", "")))) > 0, "name", "Docker Hub", "source", "dockerhub"), "name", "GHCR", "source", "ghcr")

spec.title: Registry data stale
spec.description: Time since a registry was last read successfully, shown once it passes 2 hours, for the collector read longest ago. The 2 hours assume the default hourly check. No shipped alert reads this age, so check Failed checks and the container log for the cause.

spec.title: Incomplete checks in ${span} ${spanunit}

The Loki alert RegistryStatsCollectionIncomplete reports the same checks from their log lines within 2 hours, so the two differ for a cause that logs no matching line. Registries out of step reads Unknown until a complete check, and the container log names the cause.
